title: One and two qubit playground
summary: Build a small circuit inside the published bounds and inspect every computed quantity. Nothing here is graded.
bounds_note: At most two qubits, the operations X, H, Z, CNOT and CZ, at most 100 operations, and at most 1024 shots. These are limits of this application, not claims about hardware.

presets.title: Bell pair
presets.description: H on q0, then CNOT with q0 controlling q1. This prepares (|00> + |11>)/sqrt(2).

presets.title: Two independent coins
presets.description: H on each qubit separately. Each qubit is an even coin flip, and the two results are independent.

presets.title: H, Z, H
presets.description: The Chapter 1 interference circuit, from |0> to |1>.

entanglement_guidance.heading: How to tell entanglement from a matching histogram
entanglement_guidance.body_markdown:
Two qubits that always agree do **not** by themselves demonstrate entanglement. A classical pair of coins glued together would do the same.

What distinguishes them is the **reduced state** of each qubit. For a Bell pair the reduced state of each qubit is maximally mixed: its density matrix is I/2 and its Bloch vector has length zero. Each qubit still has a local state; it is a mixed one, and the pair has a joint state that does not factor into two separate qubit states.

For a **verified pure** bipartite joint state, a mixed reduced state does establish entanglement. That reasoning does not extend to an arbitrary mixed joint state, where a mixed local state alone proves nothing. This laboratory knows the joint state exactly because it computed it, so the statement it makes is sound here.

Compare the two presets above. **Two independent coins** and **Bell pair** give the same even marginals on each qubit. Only the Bell pair has mixed reduced states.

sources.title: Multiple-system quantum information - IBM Quantum Learning

bloch_note: A Bloch sphere represents one qubit. Local spheres for an entangled register do not encode the joint state. A pure single-qubit state lies on the surface; a mixed one lies inside.
prerequisite_note: The playground is open to everyone. Chapter 3 teaches two-qubit states properly; this is a place to look, not a graded activity.
